summary: Figure tex18 traces a concrete run of the 5-comparator sorting network the paper uses to sort rates inside its one-shot max-min fair optimization. Four input wires f1-f4 start with the values 9, 6, 4, and 8, each kept in its own colour (red, green, blue, orange) as it moves through the network. Two comparators run first (f1-f2 and f3-f4), each sending its smaller input up and its larger input down; then two more (f1-f3 and f2-f4); then a final one (f2-f3), always following the min/max rule shown in the small legend: the upper wire gets min(x1,x2), the lower gets max(x1,x2). After all five comparisons, the four colours sort themselves ascending onto outputs t1-t4 as 4, 6, 8, 9.
